headline: Living Thoughts.
lede: Quinelings are programs with animated mathematical bodies. Give one a task, run it with your data, and explore the calculation inside its form.
labIntro: Choose a task and try a change. Run both inputs, then select an operation to see what it calculated and where it appears in the body.
replayIntro: Replay opens the saved result. Run the comparison calculates both inputs again.
ownershipIntro: Each operation owns a region of the body. Select an operation below to highlight its region and inspect its inputs.
bodyLegend: Color identifies an operation’s role. Gold labels show recorded values; lines connect the selected operation to its inputs. Motion changes the pose.
metricsHelp: Changed values count differences between the two runs. Anatomy change measures corresponding body points at a fixed pose. Input changes keep the same body; editing the program creates a new source. Interpreter requests count attempts to run a task.
sourceTitle: Change the rule. Change the body.
sourceIntro: These readings add up to seven liters. Add a five-liter limit and the result becomes five. The new operation gets its own region in the body.
retryIntro: The supplied outcomes are retry, retry, then success. One attempt stops at the first retry. Four attempts reach success on the third. Set a limit and compare.
quineIntro: A quine emits its own complete source. Each Quineling has a constructor that does this, so a new instance can be built from the source it produces.
genomeIntro: The same source can be stored as wave coefficients or exact RGB values. These data records contain the complete program; a picture of the creature does not.
generationIntro: Recover three generations to build and run successive copies with the same inputs. Each copy is checked against the original source and result.
conceptBody: Start with a task: “Find a route around the closed road.” Express it in QDL as typed operations and their connections. The interpreter reads the supplied observations, runs each operation when its inputs are ready, and records the result.
thoughtBody: QDL makes the task explicit: what it observes, what it computes and what action it proposes. You can inspect the program and every recorded step.
noveltyBody: The source also describes an anatomy made from mathematical curves. Operations are assigned regions, colors group their roles, and connections show how values flow. The renderer animates this anatomy; the interpreter runs the task when you press Run.
furtherBody: Write a typed task in the workspace, or connect an agent through the TypeScript SDK, MCP or A2A. In the Ranch, combine compatible programs and explore inherited bodies.
